input.new_string:
**2026-09-20 — milestone: first confirmed successful real autonomous drive to a SPU-BERT goal on the physical Jackal, end to end.** After all the fixes above (IMU units, route-caching, RViz CPU), `/spu_bert/enable_motion` armed, robot drove in intermittent bursts (v up to ~0.25 m/s, heading_error mostly <0.08 rad, tracking a shrinking Nav2 global path 119->20 poses) and the bridge/tracker logged `hold:goal_reached` / `goal_reached_disarmed` on arrival, auto-disarming itself cleanly with no manual intervention needed. RC/e-stop held ready throughout per standing safety practice.

**2026-09-20 — RViz's `Frame Rate` setting (`Global Options` in the .rviz file) matters a lot on this host's forced-software-rendering setup: 30fps drove rviz2 to 328-641% CPU (3-6+ cores) continuously, even with a fairly light Displays list (Grid/TF/Map/LaserScan/Path/MarkerArray, no PointCloud2 or camera Image display).** This alone measurably degraded `/aft_mapped_to_init` (odom) publish health (max gap dropped from ~0.9s to ~0.5s after the fix) by starving other processes on the box (host load average dropped from 16.59 to ~2-3 once both this and the memory leak below were fixed). Dropping `Frame Rate: 30` to `Frame Rate: 3` in the .rviz file cut rviz2 to ~25-33% CPU with no loss of functionality (Tools like SetGoal/SetInitialPose respond on click regardless of the passive redraw rate) - do this by default on this host rather than only when CPU-constrained. The .rviz file is a real copy in the container at `.../share/moai_jackal_spubert/rviz/real_jackal_spubert.rviz`, not bind-mounted - edit on host, `docker cp` back in, then relaunch rviz2 (with the `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE`/`GALLIUM_DRIVER` env vars from the entry above) to pick it up.

**2026-09-20 — second, separate FAST-LIVO memory leak found and root-caused (distinct from the 09-16 `img_buffer`/`feat_map` ones, which remain correctly fixed and were NOT the cause here): `vio.cpp`'s `Feature::img_` retains a full-frame (shallow-copy, refcount-shared) image reference per feature, and `slideFeatMap()`'s distance-gated pruning (`feat_map_sliding_thresh`, was 8m, tried lowering to 2m) does essentially nothing to bound it in a lab-scale test where the robot never travels that far.** Confirmed via a fresh heaptrack run (same method as the 09-16 entry, same launch `prefix=` env var mechanism): peak consumer was 632MB over 694 calls from `cv::cvtColor` called inside `VIOManager::processFrame` (`vio.cpp:1861`, the in-place `BGR2GRAY` conversion) - NOT `img_cbk`/`img_buffer` this time, which stayed a healthy 8MB, confirming the 09-16 fix is still working. Traced the retention to `vio.cpp:931` and `:1010` (`ftr_new->img_ = img;`, a shallow assignment, not `.clone()`) inside the feature-creation code that runs on essentially every tracked feature every frame - each `Feature` object keeps its originating frame's full image buffer alive via shared refcount for as long as that feature survives in a `VisualPoint`'s `obs_` list, and since pruning is purely spatial, a stationary or slow-moving robot (true of most lab tests) never prunes old features/frames at all, so RSS grows ~250-700MB/min with no bound, accelerating as CPU cost grows with the retained working set. **This looks structural to the algorithm's patch-matching design (`Feature::img_` is read back for `warpAffine`-based affine-compensated photometric matching in `vio.cpp:791,1196,1335` - not dead/removable code) and needs an actual bounded-history fix (e.g. cap observations per `VisualPoint`, or store only the small warped patch instead of the whole frame) to be done properly - not attempted under time pressure this session.**

**2026-09-20 — operational workaround adopted for this leak, likely to be the right permanent choice for this deployment anyway: disable VIO/image processing entirely and run LIO-only, via `fast_livo_image_enable:=false` on `full_stack.launch.py` (no code change, no rebuild).** Confirmed: no more `[ VIO ]` log lines, RSS flat at ~145-150MB over an extended stationary check (was climbing to 1GB+ within a minute with VIO on), `[ LIO ]` feature counts stayed healthy (effective ~4400-4500). Rationale beyond just dodging the bug: **this robot always operates in a known, fixed, already-mapped lab environment (AMCL localizes against a pre-built static map), not an unfamiliar/dynamic one** - VIO's main value-add (visual feature richness for robustness in geometrically-degenerate or unfamiliar scenes) isn't needed here; LIO+AMCL-against-a-known-map is the standard, sufficient architecture for this use case. Treat `fast_livo_image_enable:=false` as the default for lab testing on this map, not just a stopgap - revisit only if a future deployment needs to localize/map in a genuinely new or highly dynamic space.

**2026-09-20 — still-unresolved, separate from all memory issues above: `/scan` (from `pointcloud_to_laserscan_node`, fed by `filterpass.py`'s output) intermittently gaps well past the tracker's 0.5-0.6s `scan_timeout_sec`/`odom_timeout_sec` (observed gaps up to 1.7-2.6s), causing the "drives a bit, holds, drives a bit" pattern even after the VIO leak and RViz CPU fixes brought host load down from 16.59 to ~2-3.** Confirmed NOT a compute/CPU problem at the affected nodes: raw `/livox/lidar` stays healthy (~8.8-9.7Hz, tight jitter) all the way through, and `filterpass.py`/`pointcloud_to_laserscan_node` both show low CPU (2-8%) and a normal sleeping process state even during observed gaps - the delay is being introduced somewhere in message delivery/scheduling (DDS/QoS-level), not in either node's own processing time. This is the same family of issue as the 09-16 `filterpass.py` fix (which cut the max gap from ~3.6s to ~1.2s but explicitly "did not fully eliminate the holds") - still not root-caused. Robot DOES still reach goals despite this (confirmed end-to-end success same day), so it's a smoothness/UX issue, not a hard blocker, but worth a proper DDS-level investigation (QoS profile mismatch, executor threading model in `pointcloud_to_laserscan_node`, or the static-unicast FastDDS discovery profile's runtime overhead) next time there's room to dig, rather than the CPU-load angle already ruled out here.

See also [[project_frodobot_sdk]] for the unrelated Frodobot data-collection pipeline.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	import array
     3	import math
     4	import numpy as np
     5	import rclpy
     6	from rclpy.node import Node
     7	from sensor_msgs.msg import PointCloud2
     8	from std_msgs.msg import Header
     9	
    10	# --- We no longer need these ---
    11	# from rclpy.qos import QoSProfile, ReliabilityPolicy, DurabilityPolicy
    12	
    13	try:
    14	    from sensor_msgs_py import point_cloud2 as pc2
    15	except Exception as e:
    16	    raise RuntimeError(
    17	        "sensor_msgs_py.point_cloud2 is required. Install 'ros-<distro>-sensor-msgs-py'."
    18	    ) from e
    19	
    20	
    21	class LidarCombinedFilter(Node):
    22	    def __init__(self):
    23	        super().__init__('lidar_combined_filter')
    24	        self.declare_parameter('input_topic', '/livox/lidar')
    25	        self.declare_parameter('output_topic', '/livox/lidar_filtered')
    26	        self.declare_parameter('angle_deg', 360.0)
    27	        self.declare_parameter('keep_within', True)
    28	        self.declare_parameter('min_intensity', 1.0)
    29	        self.declare_parameter('max_intensity', 255.0)
    30	        input_topic = self.get_parameter('input_topic').get_parameter_value().string_value
    31	        output_topic = self.get_parameter('output_topic').get_parameter_value().string_value
    32	        self.angle_rad = math.radians(self.get_parameter('angle_deg').get_parameter_value().double_value)
    33	        self.keep_within = self.get_parameter('keep_within').get_parameter_value().bool_value
    34	        self.min_intensity = self.get_parameter('min_intensity').get_parameter_value().double_value
    35	        self.max_intensity = self.get_parameter('max_intensity').get_parameter_value().double_value
    36	        # The angle gate is a no-op once the window already covers the full
    37	        # circle (the common default) -- skip the per-point trig in that case.
    38	        self._angle_is_noop = self.keep_within and self.angle_rad >= math.pi
    39	        self.sub = self.create_subscription(PointCloud2, input_topic, self.pc_callback, 10)
    40	
    41	        self.pub = self.create_publisher(PointCloud2, output_topic, 10)
    42	
    43	        self.get_logger().info(
    44	            f"Subscribed to: {input_topic}\n"
    45	            f"Publishing to: {output_topic}\n"
    46	            f"Angle: ±{math.degrees(self.angle_rad):.1f}°, keep_within={self.keep_within}\n"
    47	            f"Intensity range: {self.min_intensity}–{self.max_intensity}\n"
    48	            f"QoS: System Default (Auto-negotiating)\n"
    49	            f"Point processing: vectorized (numpy)"
    50	        )
    51	
    52	    def pc_callback(self, msg: PointCloud2):
    53	        field_names = [f.name for f in msg.fields]
    54	        if 'x' not in field_names or 'y' not in field_names:
    55	            self.get_logger().warn("No 'x' or 'y' field — republishing original.")
    56	            self.pub.publish(msg)
    57	            return
    58	
    59	        total_count = msg.width * msg.height
    60	        if total_count == 0:
    61	            self.pub.publish(msg)
    62	            return
    63	
    64	        # Structured view straight over the raw bytes -- no per-point Python
    65	        # objects, no per-point math. This is what made the old row-by-row
    66	        # loop unable to keep up with the LiDAR's point rate (thousands of
    67	        # points per frame at 10Hz), causing multi-second gaps downstream.
    68	        dtype = pc2.dtype_from_fields(msg.fields, point_step=msg.point_step)
    69	        points = np.frombuffer(msg.data, dtype=dtype, count=total_count)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
: "${IMAGE:?Set IMAGE to the versioned stability overlay image}"
: "${CAPSTONE_CALIB:?Set CAPSTONE_CALIB to the existing lab calibration directory}"
if [[ "$(docker image inspect --format '{{index .Config.Labels "org.moai.stability.overlay"}}' "$IMAGE")" != true ]]; then
  echo "IMAGE is not a stability overlay built by build_stability_overlay.bash" >&2
  exit 1
fi
export IMAGE CAPSTONE_CALIB
export MOAI_RUNTIME_FROM_IMAGE=1
# Keep the original container available for rollback; select the target explicitly.
export CONTAINER_NAME="${CONTAINER_NAME:-moai_jackal_spubert_stability}"
exec bash "$SCRIPT_DIR/run_real_jackal_with_dds.bash"

set -euo pipefail

    && -s "$REPOSITORY_DIR/spu_deploy_docker/context/calib/intrinsic.txt" ]]; then
  export CAPSTONE_CALIB="$REPOSITORY_DIR/spu_deploy_docker/context/calib"
fi

exec bash "$SCRIPT_DIR/run_real_jackal_container.bash"

잠깐, 헷갈리네. `!` 명령이 정확히 어느 머신에서 실행되는지부터 확인하자. 이거만 쳐줘:

```
!hostname
```

지금 상황 파악됨 — 네가 치는 `!` 명령은 NUC(`cpr-j100-0519`)에서 실행되는데, 내가 고쳐야 하는 건 **노트북**(컨테이너/FAST-LIVO/AMCL이 실제로 도는 곳, `moai-Vector-16-HX-AI-A2XWIG`)이야. 둘이 다른 머신이었어.

노트북에 직접 접근할 방법이 있어? (물리적으로 그 앞에 있거나, 다른 터미널 창이 이미 노트북에 떠 있거나) 아니면 NUC에서 노트북으로 SSH가 가능해?
좋아, 노트북 앞에 가서 터미널 열고 `!hostname` 먼저 쳐서 `moai-Vector-16-HX-AI-A2XWIG`로 나오는지 확인해줘. 확인되면 sysctl 명령 줄게.

89	
90	**2026-09-20 — second, separate FAST-LIVO memory leak found and root-caused (distinct from the 09-16 `img_buffer`/`feat_map` ones, which remain correctly fixed and were NOT the cause here): `vio.cpp`'s `Feature::img_` retains a full-frame (shallow-copy, refcount-shared) image reference per feature, and `slideFeatMap()`'s distance-gated pruning (`feat_map_sliding_thresh`, was 8m, tried lowering to 2m) does essentially nothing to bound it in a lab-scale test where the robot never travels that far.** Confirmed via a fresh heaptrack run (same method as the 09-16 entry, same launch `prefix=` env var mechanism): peak consumer was 632MB over 694 calls from `cv::cvtColor` called inside `VIOManager::processFrame` (`vio.cpp:1861`, the in-place `BGR2GRAY` conversion) - NOT `img_cbk`/`img_buffer` this time, which stayed a healthy 8MB, confirming the 09-16 fix is still working. Traced the retention to `vio.cpp:931` and `:1010` (`ftr_new->img_ = img;`, a shallow assignment, not `.clone()`) inside the feature-creation code that runs on essentially every tracked feature every frame - each `Feature` object keeps its originating frame's full image buffer alive via shared refcount for as long as that feature survives in a `VisualPoint`'s `obs_` list, and since pruning is purely spatial, a stationary or slow-moving robot (true of most lab tests) never prunes old features/frames at all, so RSS grows ~250-700MB/min with no bound, accelerating as CPU cost grows with the retained working set. **This looks structural to the algorithm's patch-matching design (`Feature::img_` is read back for `warpAffine`-based affine-compensated photometric matching in `vio.cpp:791,1196,1335` - not dead/removable code) and needs an actual bounded-history fix (e.g. cap observations per `VisualPoint`, or store only the small warped patch instead of the whole frame) to be done properly - not attempted under time pressure this session.**
91	
92	**2026-09-20 — operational workaround adopted for this leak, likely to be the right permanent choice for this deployment anyway: disable VIO/image processing entirely and run LIO-only, via `fast_livo_image_enable:=false` on `full_stack.launch.py` (no code change, no rebuild).** Confirmed: no more `[ VIO ]` log lines, RSS flat at ~145-150MB over an extended stationary check (was climbing to 1GB+ within a minute with VIO on), `[ LIO ]` feature counts stayed healthy (effective ~4400-4500). Rationale beyond just dodging the bug: **this robot always operates in a known, fixed, already-mapped lab environment (AMCL localizes against a pre-built static map), not an unfamiliar/dynamic one** - VIO's main value-add (visual feature richness for robustness in geometrically-degenerate or unfamiliar scenes) isn't needed here; LIO+AMCL-against-a-known-map is the standard, sufficient architecture for this use case. Treat `fast_livo_image_enable:=false` as the default for lab testing on this map, not just a stopgap - revisit only if a future deployment needs to localize/map in a genuinely new or highly dynamic space.

**2026-09-20 — flagged unresolved, then 2026-09-21 ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED: the `/scan` stop-go jitter was the laptop host's default Linux UDP receive buffer being far too small for this DDS traffic volume.** `netstat -su` showed `receive buffer errors` climbing at roughly 15% of all UDP packets received (e.g. 901700 of 5783058) - the kernel was silently dropping datagrams because `net.core.rmem_default` was the Ubuntu default `212992` bytes (~208KB), too small for the burst of PointCloud2/Image/IMU traffic this stack pushes through one NIC. This is exactly why the CPU-load investigation on 09-20 (ruling out `filterpass.py`/`pointcloud_to_laserscan_node` compute time, which was correct as far as it went) never found the cause - it's a kernel-level socket buffer limit, invisible to `ps`/CPU%, and invisible to `ip -s link` (that only shows NIC-level drops, not per-socket UDP buffer overflow - always check `netstat -su`'s "receive buffer errors" specifically, not just interface stats, when ROS2 topics have mysterious gaps with healthy CPU). Fixed on the **laptop host** (not the NUC, not the container - `net.core.*` is host-kernel-wide, and Docker containers share the host's kernel/network stack unless given a separate netns) via:
```
sudo sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=67108864 net.core.rmem_default=67108864 \
  net.core.wmem_max=67108864 net.core.wmem_default=67108864 \
  net.core.netdev_max_backlog=4096
```
**Existing already-open sockets don't pick up a new `rmem_default` - the whole ROS2 pipeline (livox driver through the SPU-BERT bridge) had to be killed and relaunched for new sockets to actually use the larger buffers.** After restart: `/scan` went from ~1.7-2.6s max gaps at an unstable ~2Hz average to a rock-solid **10.00Hz with 0.098-0.102s min/max (essentially the sensor's own jitter, i.e. perfect)**. This setting does not persist across a laptop reboot (sysctl -w is runtime-only) - add it to `/etc/sysctl.d/` if this keeps recurring across sessions; noted here for now, not yet made persistent.

**2026-09-21 — critical durability gotcha, confirmed the hard way: the `moai-jackal-spubert:stability-fbff8b3-lab1` base image predates essentially all of the FAST-LIVO/filterpass/RViz fixes above, and the stability container is `--rm` (deleted on `docker stop` or host reboot) - so EVERY fresh container recreation loses ALL of the following and they must be manually reapplied before trusting the stack:**
- `livox_ros_driver2/src/lddc.cpp` IMU units fix (g -> m/s^2) - not in either git repo, container-filesystem-only; recreate by `docker exec cat`-ing it out (NOT `docker cp`, see below), editing, copying back in, `colcon build --packages-select livox_ros_driver2` inside the container.
- `mola_bringup/filterpass.py`'s vectorized numpy fix (09-16) - the base image has the OLD per-point-Python-loop version, which pegged CPU at 60-70% (vs 2-13% for the fixed version) and contributed to (but, per the 09-21 finding above, was NOT the sole cause of) `/scan` jitter. This one IS committed in the `spu_deploy_docker` git repo (`context/local_pkgs/mola_bringup/{mola_bringup,scripts}/filterpass.py`) - `docker cp` it into all 4 on-disk copies inside the container (`src/mola_bringup/{scripts,mola_bringup}/filterpass.py` and `install/mola_bringup/{local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages,lib}/mola_bringup/filterpass.py`).
- FAST-LIVO's `local_map.sliding_thresh`/`half_map_size` launch-param overrides in `mapping_mid360.launch.py` (this base image predates even the *existence* of these params in `voxel_map.cpp`/`vio.cpp` - grepping the container's own installed launch file for `sliding_thresh` returns nothing). Moot in practice as long as `fast_livo_image_enable:=false` (LIO-only) stays the default per the 09-20 entry above, since the leaks this bounded were both in VIO/image code paths - but don't assume the sliding-window protection is present if VIO is ever re-enabled on a freshly recreated container.
- The `.rviz` config's `Frame Rate: 3` (vs. the stale default `30`) - also container-filesystem-only, also **must be extracted with `docker exec cat <path> > file` rather than `docker cp`**, because this specific package was built with `colcon build --symlink-install` and its installed `.rviz` path is a symlink pointing into `build/`, not the file itself - `docker cp` on a symlink source just copies the (host-unresolvable, container-internal) symlink itself, silently producing a broken link on the host with a misleadingly old mtime. Copy the *fixed* file back in via `docker cp` targeting the symlink's *resolved build/ path* directly (e.g. `.../build/moai_jackal_spubert/rviz/real_jackal_spubert.rviz`), then verify through the `install/.../share/...` path that the symlink now reads through to the new content.
**General lesson: after any container recreation, re-verify each of these four independently (don't assume "the image is the stability image, so it has the stability-session fixes") - `grep`/`diff` the relevant file inside the fresh container against the git-tracked or previously-known-fixed version before trusting it.**

See also [[project_frodobot_sdk]] for the unrelated Frodobot data-collection pipeline.

This setting does not persist across a laptop reboot (sysctl -w is runtime-only) - add it to `/etc/sysctl.d/` if this keeps recurring across sessions; noted here for now, not yet made persistent.

+**2026-09-21 — critical durability gotcha, confirmed the hard way: the `moai-jackal-spubert:stability-fbff8b3-lab1` base image predates essentially all of the FAST-LIVO/filterpass/RViz fixes above, and the stability container is `--rm` (deleted on `docker stop` or host reboot) - so EVERY fresh container recreation loses ALL of the following and they must be manually reapplied before trusting the stack:**

+- `livox_ros_driver2/src/lddc.cpp` IMU units fix (g -> m/s^2) - not in either git repo, container-filesystem-only; recreate by `docker exec cat`-ing it out (NOT `docker cp`, see below), editing, copying back in, `colcon build --packages-select livox_ros_driver2` inside the container.

+- `mola_bringup/filterpass.py`'s vectorized numpy fix (09-16) - the base image has the OLD per-point-Python-loop version, which pegged CPU at 60-70% (vs 2-13% for the fixed version) and contributed to (but, per the 09-21 finding above, was NOT the sole cause of) `/scan` jitter. This one IS committed in the `spu_deploy_docker` git repo (`context/local_pkgs/mola_bringup/{mola_bringup,scripts}/filterpass.py`) - `docker cp` it into all 4 on-disk copies inside the container (`src/mola_bringup/{scripts,mola_bringup}/filterpass.py` and `install/mola_bringup/{local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages,lib}/mola_bringup/filterpass.py`).

+- FAST-LIVO's `local_map.sliding_thresh`/`half_map_size` launch-param overrides in `mapping_mid360.launch.py` (this base image predates even the *existence* of these params in `voxel_map.cpp`/`vio.cpp` - grepping the container's own installed launch file for `sliding_thresh` returns nothing). Moot in practice as long as `fast_livo_image_enable:=false` (LIO-only) stays the default per the 09-20 entry above, since the leaks this bounded were both in VIO/image code paths - but don't assume the sliding-window protection is present if VIO is ever re-enabled on a freshly recreated container.

+- The `.rviz` config's `Frame Rate: 3` (vs. the stale default `30`) - also container-filesystem-only, also **must be extracted with `docker exec cat <path> > file` rather than `docker cp`**, because this specific package was built with `colcon build --symlink-install` and its installed `.rviz` path is a symlink pointing into `build/`, not the file itself - `docker cp` on a symlink source just copies the (host-unresolvable, container-internal) symlink itself, silently producing a broken link on the host with a misleadingly old mtime. Copy the *fixed* file back in via `docker cp` targeting the symlink's *resolved build/ path* directly (e.g. `.../build/moai_jackal_spubert/rviz/real_jackal_spubert.rviz`), then verify through the `install/.../share/...` path that the symlink now reads through to the new content.

+**General lesson: after any container recreation, re-verify each of these four independently (don't assume "the image is the stability image, so it has the stability-session fixes") - `grep`/`diff` the relevant file inside the fresh container against the git-tracked or previously-known-fixed version before trusting it.**
See also [[project_frodobot_sdk]] for the unrelated Frodobot data-collection pipeline.

content.text:
**Goal 도달! 완전히 매끄럽게, 멈춤 없이 한 번에 도착했어.** `goal_reached_disarmed`로 자동 disarm까지 완료.

오늘 세션 요약:
- 네트워크 IP, NUC 클럭 동기화, 컨테이너 재생성 — 어제 픽스들(IMU 유닛, VIO 비활성화, RViz frame rate, filterpass 벡터화) 전부 재적용
- **`/scan` stop-go의 진짜 원인 발견: 노트북 커널의 UDP 수신 버퍼가 너무 작아서(~208KB) 패킷의 15%가 드롭되고 있었음.** `net.core.rmem_default` 등을 64MB로 올리고 파이프라인 재시작 → `/scan`이 완벽한 10.00Hz로 안정화
- 그 결과 이번 주행은 hold 한 번도 없이 처음부터 끝까지 매끄럽게 완주

메모리에 전부 기록해둠 (특히 stability 컨테이너가 `--rm`이라 재생성될 때마다 사라지는 4가지 픽스 체크리스트 — 다음에 컨테이너 새로 켤 때 꼭 확인).
/etc 쓰기는 sudo 필요해서 내가 직접 못 해. 노트북 터미널에 이거 그대로 실행해줘:

input.command:
cat <<'EOF'
sudo tee /etc/sysctl.d/99-jackal-dds-udp-buffers.conf <<'CONF'
# Increased UDP socket buffers for the real Jackal / FAST-LIVO / SPU-BERT
# ROS2 DDS stack. The Ubuntu default (net.core.rmem_default=212992, ~208KB)
# was too small for this traffic volume, causing ~15% UDP receive buffer
# errors (visible via `netstat -su`) and multi-second /scan gaps despite
# healthy CPU everywhere. See project_capstone_navi_jackal memory,
# 2026-09-21 entry, for the full diagnosis.
net.core.rmem_max=67108864
net.core.rmem_default=67108864
net.core.wmem_max=67108864
net.core.wmem_default=67108864
net.core.netdev_max_backlog=4096
CONF
sudo sysctl --system
EOF

message.content: 했어 . 근데 지금 다른 팀들 설정을 바꾸는건아니지?

content.text:
좋은 질문이야, 정직하게 답할게 — 이건 **머신 전체 커널 설정**이라 노트북에 로그인된 다른 사용자/프로세스에도 다 적용돼. 우리 ROS2 스택만 골라서 바꾸는 방법은 없어(도커 컨테이너도 호스트 커널을 공유하니까).

실제 영향은:
- `rmem_max`/`wmem_max`는 **상한선**만 올린 거라, 다른 프로세스가 큰 버퍼를 요청했을 때 더 받을 수 있게 해주는 것뿐 — 아무도 강제로 더 많은 메모리를 쓰게 되진 않음
- `rmem_default`/`wmem_default`는 **기본값**을 올린 거라, 명시적으로 버퍼 크기를 지정 안 하는 소켓(주로 UDP)들이 이제 더 큰 기본 버퍼를 씀. TCP는 자체 autotuning(tcp_rmem/tcp_wmem)을 쓰니까 이건 안 건드렸음
- `netdev_max_backlog`는 NIC 패킷 큐 깊이라 늘리면 오히려 다른 사람 트래픽도 드롭 덜 됨

즉, 로보틱스/고처리량 네트워킹 환경에서 흔히 쓰는 표준적인 튜닝이고, 다른 팀 작업을 방해할 가능성은 거의 없어 — 오히려 UDP 쓰는 다른 작업이 있다면 걔들한테도 도움 될 수 있음. 혹시 이 랩 머신에 다른 팀이 의도적으로 낮은 버퍼값을 설정해둔 특별한 이유가 있었다면 확인해보는 게 좋겠지만, 일반적으론 안전한 변경이야.

content.text:
이 시스템은 실제로 회피를 시도해 — `all_candidates_rejected`/`adaptive_guidance_failed` 로그가 바로 그거야: 여러 회피 후보 경로를 생성해서 로봇 몸체(footprint)가 안전하게 지나갈 수 있는지 하나씩 검사하는데, **지금 이 지점에서는 시도한 후보 중 안전하게 통과 가능한 게 하나도 없어서** 억지로 밀고 가지 않고 멈춘 거야. 억지로 통과시키게 만드는 건 실제 충돌 위험을 감수하는 거라 안전장치를 우회하는 셋팅이라 함부로 바꾸긴 좀 그래.

실제로 통과 가능한 폭이 있는지가 관건인데:
1. 장애물이 사람이면 비켜달라고 하거나
2. 장애물이 치울 수 있는 물건이면 옆으로 치우거나
3. 로봇이 지나가기엔 통로가 너무 좁은 구조적 문제일 수도 있음 (로봇 폭 + 안전마진 대비)

지금 장애물 상황이 어떤 거야? (사람/물건, 통로 폭 느낌)

def generate_launch_description():
    package_share = get_package_share_directory("moai_jackal_spubert")
    default_config = f"{package_share}/config/real_jackal_social005.yaml"
    default_rviz_config = f"{package_share}/rviz/real_jackal_spubert.rviz"

    config_file = LaunchConfiguration("config_file")
    cmd_vel_topic = LaunchConfiguration("cmd_vel_topic")
    use_cuda = LaunchConfiguration("use_cuda")
    require_global_path = LaunchConfiguration("require_global_path")
    launch_rviz = LaunchConfiguration("launch_rviz")
    rviz_config = LaunchConfiguration("rviz_config")
    route_progress_ambiguity_distance_m = LaunchConfiguration(
        "route_progress_ambiguity_distance_m"
    )

    bridge = Node(
        package="moai_jackal_spubert",
        executable="real_jackal_spubert_bridge",
        name="real_jackal_spubert_bridge",
        output="screen",
        parameters=[
            config_file,
            {
                "use_cuda": use_cuda,
                "require_global_path": require_global_path,
                "route_progress_ambiguity_distance_m": ParameterValue(
                    route_progress_ambiguity_distance_m, value_type=float
                ),
            },
        ],
    )
    tracker = Node(
        package="moai_jackal_spubert",
        executable="safe_path_tracker",
        name="safe_path_tracker",
        output="screen",
        parameters=[config_file, {"cmd_vel_topic": cmd_vel_topic, "motion_enabled": False}],
    )
    rviz = Node(
        package="rviz2",
        executable="rviz2",
        name="spubert_navigation_rviz",
        output="screen",

            ),
            bridge,

            rviz,
        ]
    )

확인해보니 `tgp_top_k`는 이미 뽑아놓은 후보 풀(`d_sample: 40`) 중에서 몇 개를 최종적으로 쓸지 정하는 값이야 — 즉 **40개 샘플 중에도 안전한 게 하나도 없으면 top_k를 8로 늘려도 의미가 없어.** 진짜 다양성을 늘리려면 `d_sample`을 늘려야 하는데, 그래도 모델이 "복도에서 큰 물체를 크게 돌아가는" 경로 자체를 잘 안 뽑는 경향이 있다면(학습 데이터 분포 문제) 근본적으로 한계가 있을 수 있어.

`d_sample`을 40→80 정도로 한번 늘려서 재시도해볼 수 있는데, 이게 통로가 진짜 좁아서 물리적으로 필요한 폭(로봇 0.34m + 안전마진 0.16m = 0.5m 클리어런스)이 안 나오는 상황이면 이것도 안 될 가능성이 있어. 시도해볼까, 아니면 지금은 RC로 바로 우회하는 게 나을까?

content.text:
구조적으로 보면 진짜 해법은 하나 있어: **지금 이 시스템엔 "모델이 실패했을 때"의 대안이 없어.** SPU-BERT 후보들이 전부 막히면 그냥 멈추기만 하고, 전통적인 로컬 플래너(장애물 감지되면 옆으로 살짝 offset해서 우회 경로 만드는 것 같은) 백업이 없음. `d_sample`/`top_k`는 같은 모델이 뽑는 후보 안에서 고르는 거라 한계가 있고.

실질적인 해법은: **후보가 전부 실패했을 때만 작동하는 "간단한 좌우 offset 탐색" 폴백을 추가하는 것.** 이미 있는 안전 체크 함수(`validate_candidate_path`, footprint 충돌 검사)를 재사용해서, 글로벌 경로를 좌/우로 조금씩 밀어보면서(0.1m, 0.2m, ...) 안전한 지점을 찾는 방식이야 — 새 플래너를 통째로 만드는 게 아니라 지금 있는 안전판정 로직 위에 탐색 루프만 얹는 거라 비교적 작은 범위의 작업.

근데 이건 진짜 로봇 안전에 관여하는 새 로직이라, 지금 이 자리에서 급하게 짜서 바로 실차에 태우는 건 안전하지 않다고 생각해 — 다음에 시간 내서 제대로 설계하고 테스트 환경에서 먼저 검증한 뒤에 넣는 게 맞을 것 같아. 지금은 RC로 우회하는 걸로 진행하자.

This setting does not persist across a laptop reboot (sysctl -w is runtime-only) - add it to `/etc/sysctl.d/` if this keeps recurring across sessions; noted here for now, not yet made persistent.
101	
102	**2026-09-21 — critical durability gotcha, confirmed the hard way: the `moai-jackal-spubert:stability-fbff8b3-lab1` base image predates essentially all of the FAST-LIVO/filterpass/RViz fixes above, and the stability container is `--rm` (deleted on `docker stop` or host reboot) - so EVERY fresh container recreation loses ALL of the following and they must be manually reapplied before trusting the stack:**
103	- `livox_ros_driver2/src/lddc.cpp` IMU units fix (g -> m/s^2) - not in either git repo, container-filesystem-only; recreate by `docker exec cat`-ing it out (NOT `docker cp`, see below), editing, copying back in, `colcon build --packages-select livox_ros_driver2` inside the container.
104	- `mola_bringup/filterpass.py`'s vectorized numpy fix (09-16) - the base image has the OLD per-point-Python-loop version, which pegged CPU at 60-70% (vs 2-13% for the fixed version) and contributed to (but, per the 09-21 finding above, was NOT the sole cause of) `/scan` jitter. This one IS committed in the `spu_deploy_docker` git repo (`context/local_pkgs/mola_bringup/{mola_bringup,scripts}/filterpass.py`) - `docker cp` it into all 4 on-disk copies inside the container (`src/mola_bringup/{scripts,mola_bringup}/filterpass.py` and `install/mola_bringup/{local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages,lib}/mola_bringup/filterpass.py`).
105	- FAST-LIVO's `local_map.sliding_thresh`/`half_map_size` launch-param overrides in `mapping_mid360.launch.py` (this base image predates even the *existence* of these params in `voxel_map.cpp`/`vio.cpp` - grepping the container's own installed launch file for `sliding_thresh` returns nothing). Moot in practice as long as `fast_livo_image_enable:=false` (LIO-only) stays the default per the 09-20 entry above, since the leaks this bounded were both in VIO/image code paths - but don't assume the sliding-window protection is present if VIO is ever re-enabled on a freshly recreated container.

- `livox_ros_driver2/src/lddc.cpp` IMU units fix (g -> m/s^2) - not in either git repo, container-filesystem-only; recreate by `docker exec cat`-ing it out (NOT `docker cp`, see below), editing, copying back in, `colcon build --packages-select livox_ros_driver2` inside the container.
- `mola_bringup/filterpass.py`'s vectorized numpy fix (09-16) - the base image has the OLD per-point-Python-loop version, which pegged CPU at 60-70% (vs 2-13% for the fixed version) and contributed to (but, per the 09-21 finding above, was NOT the sole cause of) `/scan` jitter. This one IS committed in the `spu_deploy_docker` git repo (`context/local_pkgs/mola_bringup/{mola_bringup,scripts}/filterpass.py`) - `docker cp` it into all 4 on-disk copies inside the container (`src/mola_bringup/{scripts,mola_bringup}/filterpass.py` and `install/mola_bringup/{local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages,lib}/mola_bringup/filterpass.py`).
- FAST-LIVO's `local_map.sliding_thresh`/`half_map_size` launch-param overrides in `mapping_mid360.launch.py` (this base image predates even the *existence* of these params in `voxel_map.cpp`/`vio.cpp` - grepping the container's own installed launch file for `sliding_thresh` returns nothing). Moot in practice as long as `fast_livo_image_enable:=false` (LIO-only) stays the default per the 09-20 entry above, since the leaks this bounded were both in VIO/image code paths - but don't assume the sliding-window protection is present if VIO is ever re-enabled on a freshly recreated container.

105	- FAST-LIVO's `local_map.sliding_thresh`/`half_map_size` launch-param overrides in `mapping_mid360.launch.py` (this base image predates even the *existence* of these params in `voxel_map.cpp`/`vio.cpp` - grepping the container's own installed launch file for `sliding_thresh` returns nothing). 106	- The `.rviz` config's `Frame Rate: 3` (vs. the stale default `30`) - also container-filesystem-only, also **must be extracted with `docker exec cat <path> > file` rather than `docker cp`**, because this specific package was built with `colcon build --symlink-install` and its installed `.rviz` path is a symlink pointing into `build/`, not the file itself - `docker cp` on a symlink source just copies the (host-unresolvable, container-internal) symlink itself, silently producing a broken link on the host with a misleadingly old mtime. input.new_string:
- **A fifth item, found later the same day: the entire `moai_jackal_spubert` package source under `/root/moai_stability_ws/src` is ALSO stale on a fresh container** (missing the 09-20 `_route_in_frame` caching fix, `route_progress_ambiguity_distance_m`, and everything else added to the `capstone_navi_stability_20260916` git clone) - this one isn't a single file, it's the whole package. Fix: `docker cp <host_repo>/real_jackal/ros2_ws/src/moai_jackal_spubert/moai_jackal_spubert/. <container>:/root/moai_stability_ws/src/moai_jackal_spubert/moai_jackal_spubert/` and same for `launch/` (**note the trailing `/.` on the source path** - `docker cp srcdir container:destdir` without it copies srcdir as a new subdirectory *inside* destdir instead of merging its contents, silently leaving the old files untouched one level up; this bit us once this session, caught by comparing line counts before/after), then `colcon build --packages-select moai_jackal_spubert` inside the container.

**General lesson: after any container recreation, re-verify each of these five independently (don't assume "the image is the stability image, so it has the stability-session fixes") - `grep`/`diff` the relevant file inside the fresh container against the git-tracked or previously-known-fixed version before trusting it.**

**2026-09-21 — pulling a newer `moai_jackal_spubert` package source into an older container can break on a missing message dependency: `real_jackal_spubert_bridge_node.py` imports `moai_nav_msgs.msg.Tracks` (pedestrian-tracking support), which isn't part of `moai_stability_ws` - it's built separately under `/root/robot_ws` (alongside `mid360_perception`/`pedestrian_tracker_node`).** Launching the bridge after a source sync crashed with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'moai_nav_msgs'` until `/root/robot_ws/install/setup.bash` was also sourced (in addition to `moai_stability_ws/install/setup.bash`) before `ros2 launch`. Always source both workspaces together for the SPU-BERT bridge on this container.

**2026-09-21 — real limitation found and worked around during actual driving: the safe_path_tracker/bridge has no fallback when SPU-BERT's candidate trajectories are all rejected near a static obstacle - it just holds forever, it does not attempt an independent local re-route.** Symptom: `hold:all_candidates_rejected:robot_footprint_collision` followed by `hold:adaptive_guidance_failed:no directly footprint-safe guidance point on global path`, persisting indefinitely (path pose count frozen, no recovery) when a single-sided obstacle (e.g. an object against one wall of a corridor) leaves no candidate with the required `footprint_radius` clearance (`robot_radius: 0.34` + `static_safety_margin: 0.16` = 0.5m). Root cause chain, traced in `guided_spubert_runtime.py`: the model draws `d_sample: 40` goal samples from its learned distribution, `goal_candidate_policy: preserve_safe_samples` tries to substitute any unsafe top-`tgp_top_k` picks with safe ones from that same 40-sample pool, and only the *final* `tgp_top_k` (declared as a rclpy param, default 5, now exposed as a launch arg alongside `route_progress_ambiguity_distance_m` - both in `real_jackal_spubert.launch.py`, committed `5a9900b`) get validated against the footprint check. **Raising `tgp_top_k` alone (tried 5->8) does nothing if the underlying 40-sample pool itself has no wide-enough-swinging sample** - confirmed empirically: worked for one obstacle encounter that same session, failed for a second, different one (a "large" object leaving less clearance). No latency concern found with `tgp_top_k=8` - candidate count only affects the trajectory-decoding tail of one model forward pass, not the (expensive) encoder, confirmed by unchanged ~100ms control-loop cadence in the logs.
**The actual fix identified (not yet implemented - real robot safety logic, needs design + bench testing before trusting it live, per the standing "don't rush safety-critical code onto the physical robot" practice): add a fallback path source that engages only when `all_candidates_rejected`/`adaptive_guidance_failed` fires - a simple lateral-offset sweep of the current global-path segment (try +/-0.1m, +/-0.2m, ... sideways from the robot), reusing the *existing* `validate_candidate_path`/footprint-collision-check machinery already in `guided_spubert_runtime.py`/`navigation_core.py` rather than writing a new local planner from scratch.** This is the same underlying idea as the "crude global-path-following fallback" floated as a last resort on 09-20, scoped down to just the obstacle-avoidance failure mode rather than replacing the whole SPU-BERT path. Operational workaround for now: RC/joystick the robot a short distance past the obstruction (re-localize with a fresh `2D Pose Estimate` after, per the standing safety practice - odom itself doesn't need a restart, just AMCL's pose belief), then resume - worked twice this session.

**2026-09-21 — second and third confirmed successful real autonomous drive-to-goal runs, after the `/scan` UDP fix**: one long run (~935-1553 poses depending on goal) tracked completely smoothly with zero holds end to end; a second, longer run hit the corridor-obstacle limitation above partway through, recovered via manual RC bypass + re-localize, then reached goal cleanly on the SPU-BERT/tracker side once past the obstruction. Net status at end of day: localization, memory stability, and sensor-pipeline timing are all solid; the one remaining known gap for unattended operation is the no-fallback-on-candidate-rejection behavior just above.

See also [[project_frodobot_sdk]] for the unrelated Frodobot data-collection pipeline.

lines: Real robot: Clearpath Jackal (namespace `j100_0519`), NUC at `administrator@192.168.50.2`, driven from laptop via docker container `moai_jackal_spubert` (image `moai-jackal-spubert:social005`), repo `/home/moai/capstone_navi`.

- `mola_bringup/filterpass.py`'s vectorized numpy fix (09-16) - the base image has the OLD per-point-Python-loop version, which pegged CPU at 60-70% (vs 2-13% for the fixed version) and contributed to (but, per the 09-21 finding above, was NOT the sole cause of) `/scan` jitter. This one IS committed in the `spu_deploy_docker` git repo (`context/local_pkgs/mola_bringup/{mola_bringup,scripts}/filterpass.py`) - `docker cp` it into all 4 on-disk copies inside the container (`src/mola_bringup/{scripts,mola_bringup}/filterpass.py` and `install/mola_bringup/{local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages,lib}/mola_bringup/filterpass.py`).

- FAST-LIVO's `local_map.sliding_thresh`/`half_map_size` launch-param overrides in `mapping_mid360.launch.py` (this base image predates even the *existence* of these params in `voxel_map.cpp`/`vio.cpp` - grepping the container's own installed launch file for `sliding_thresh` returns nothing). Moot in practice as long as `fast_livo_image_enable:=false` (LIO-only) stays the default per the 09-20 entry above, since the leaks this bounded were both in VIO/image code paths - but don't assume the sliding-window protection is present if VIO is ever re-enabled on a freshly recreated container.

- The `.rviz` config's `Frame Rate: 3` (vs. the stale default `30`) - also container-filesystem-only, also **must be extracted with `docker exec cat <path> > file` rather than `docker cp`**, because this specific package was built with `colcon build --symlink-install` and its installed `.rviz` path is a symlink pointing into `build/`, not the file itself - `docker cp` on a symlink source just copies the (host-unresolvable, container-internal) symlink itself, silently producing a broken link on the host with a misleadingly old mtime. Copy the *fixed* file back in via `docker cp` targeting the symlink's *resolved build/ path* directly (e.g. `.../build/moai_jackal_spubert/rviz/real_jackal_spubert.rviz`), then verify through the `install/.../share/...` path that the symlink now reads through to the new content.

-**General lesson: after any container recreation, re-verify each of these four independently (don't assume "the image is the stability image, so it has the stability-session fixes") - `grep`/`diff` the relevant file inside the fresh container against the git-tracked or previously-known-fixed version before trusting it.**

+- **A fifth item, found later the same day: the entire `moai_jackal_spubert` package source under `/root/moai_stability_ws/src` is ALSO stale on a fresh container** (missing the 09-20 `_route_in_frame` caching fix, `route_progress_ambiguity_distance_m`, and everything else added to the `capstone_navi_stability_20260916` git clone) - this one isn't a single file, it's the whole package. Fix: `docker cp <host_repo>/real_jackal/ros2_ws/src/moai_jackal_spubert/moai_jackal_spubert/. <container>:/root/moai_stability_ws/src/moai_jackal_spubert/moai_jackal_spubert/` and same for `launch/` (**note the trailing `/.` on the source path** - `docker cp srcdir container:destdir` without it copies srcdir as a new subdirectory *inside* destdir instead of merging its contents, silently leaving the old files untouched one level up; this bit us once this session, caught by comparing line counts before/after), then `colcon build --packages-select moai_jackal_spubert` inside the container.

+**General lesson: after any container recreation, re-verify each of these five independently (don't assume "the image is the stability image, so it has the stability-session fixes") - `grep`/`diff` the relevant file inside the fresh container against the git-tracked or previously-known-fixed version before trusting it.**

+**2026-09-21 — pulling a newer `moai_jackal_spubert` package source into an older container can break on a missing message dependency: `real_jackal_spubert_bridge_node.py` imports `moai_nav_msgs.msg.Tracks` (pedestrian-tracking support), which isn't part of `moai_stability_ws` - it's built separately under `/root/robot_ws` (alongside `mid360_perception`/`pedestrian_tracker_node`).** Launching the bridge after a source sync crashed with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'moai_nav_msgs'` until `/root/robot_ws/install/setup.bash` was also sourced (in addition to `moai_stability_ws/install/setup.bash`) before `ros2 launch`. Always source both workspaces together for the SPU-BERT bridge on this container.

+**2026-09-21 — real limitation found and worked around during actual driving: the safe_path_tracker/bridge has no fallback when SPU-BERT's candidate trajectories are all rejected near a static obstacle - it just holds forever, it does not attempt an independent local re-route.** Symptom: `hold:all_candidates_rejected:robot_footprint_collision` followed by `hold:adaptive_guidance_failed:no directly footprint-safe guidance point on global path`, persisting indefinitely (path pose count frozen, no recovery) when a single-sided obstacle (e.g. an object against one wall of a corridor) leaves no candidate with the required `footprint_radius` clearance (`robot_radius: 0.34` + `static_safety_margin: 0.16` = 0.5m). Root cause chain, traced in `guided_spubert_runtime.py`: the model draws `d_sample: 40` goal samples from its learned distribution, `goal_candidate_policy: preserve_safe_samples` tries to substitute any unsafe top-`tgp_top_k` picks with safe ones from that same 40-sample pool, and only the *final* `tgp_top_k` (declared as a rclpy param, default 5, now exposed as a launch arg alongside `route_progress_ambiguity_distance_m` - both in `real_jackal_spubert.launch.py`, committed `5a9900b`) get validated against the footprint check. **Raising `tgp_top_k` alone (tried 5->8) does nothing if the underlying 40-sample pool itself has no wide-enough-swinging sample** - confirmed empirically: worked for one obstacle encounter that same session, failed for a second, different one (a "large" object leaving less clearance). No latency concern found with `tgp_top_k=8` - candidate count only affects the trajectory-decoding tail of one model forward pass, not the (expensive) encoder, confirmed by unchanged ~100ms control-loop cadence in the logs.

+**The actual fix identified (not yet implemented - real robot safety logic, needs design + bench testing before trusting it live, per the standing "don't rush safety-critical code onto the physical robot" practice): add a fallback path source that engages only when `all_candidates_rejected`/`adaptive_guidance_failed` fires - a simple lateral-offset sweep of the current global-path segment (try +/-0.1m, +/-0.2m, ... sideways from the robot), reusing the *existing* `validate_candidate_path`/footprint-collision-check machinery already in `guided_spubert_runtime.py`/`navigation_core.py` rather than writing a new local planner from scratch.** This is the same underlying idea as the "crude global-path-following fallback" floated as a last resort on 09-20, scoped down to just the obstacle-avoidance failure mode rather than replacing the whole SPU-BERT path. Operational workaround for now: RC/joystick the robot a short distance past the obstruction (re-localize with a fresh `2D Pose Estimate` after, per the standing safety practice - odom itself doesn't need a restart, just AMCL's pose belief), then resume - worked twice this session.

+**2026-09-21 — second and third confirmed successful real autonomous drive-to-goal runs, after the `/scan` UDP fix**: one long run (~935-1553 poses depending on goal) tracked completely smoothly with zero holds end to end; a second, longer run hit the corridor-obstacle limitation above partway through, recovered via manual RC bypass + re-localize, then reached goal cleanly on the SPU-BERT/tracker side once past the obstruction. Net status at end of day: localization, memory stability, and sensor-pipeline timing are all solid; the one remaining known gap for unattended operation is the no-fallback-on-candidate-rejection behavior just above.
See also [[project_frodobot_sdk]] for the unrelated Frodobot data-collection pipeline.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Build only: no container is stopped, launched or armed by this script.
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REAL_JACKAL_DIR="$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd -- "$REAL_JACKAL_DIR/.." && pwd)"
: "${BASE_IMAGE:?Set BASE_IMAGE to the audited existing deployment image ID or snapshot tag}"
PACKAGE_SOURCE="$REAL_JACKAL_DIR/ros2_ws/src/moai_jackal_spubert"

for command in docker python3 tar; do
  command -v "$command" >/dev/null || { echo "Missing command: $command" >&2; exit 1; }
done
BASE_IMAGE_ID="$(docker image inspect --format '{{.Id}}' "$BASE_IMAGE")"
# A local tag works with Dockerfile FROM across Docker/BuildKit versions, including
# when BASE_IMAGE was supplied as a bare image ID. Never retag an existing name.
BASE_PIN_TAG="moai-jackal-spubert-base:sha-${BASE_IMAGE_ID#sha256:}"
if docker image inspect "$BASE_PIN_TAG" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  [[ "$(docker image inspect --format '{{.Id}}' "$BASE_PIN_TAG")" == "$BASE_IMAGE_ID" ]] \
    || { echo "Base snapshot tag collision: $BASE_PIN_TAG" >&2; exit 1; }
else
  docker image tag "$BASE_IMAGE_ID" "$BASE_PIN_TAG"
fi
BUILD_CONTEXT="$(mktemp -d /tmp/moai_stability_build.XXXXXX)"
trap 'rm -rf -- "$BUILD_CONTEXT"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$BUILD_CONTEXT/package" "$BUILD_CONTEXT/scripts"
tar -C "$PACKAGE_SOURCE" --exclude='__pycache__' --exclude='*.pyc' \
  --exclude='test' --exclude='.pytest_cache' -cf - . \
  | tar -C "$BUILD_CONTEXT/package" -xf -
cp "$REAL_JACKAL_DIR/scripts/"*.bash "$BUILD_CONTEXT/scripts/"
cp "$REAL_JACKAL_DIR/scripts/"*.py "$BUILD_CONTEXT/scripts/"
cp "$SCRIPT_DIR/Dockerfile.stability" "$BUILD_CONTEXT/Dockerfile"
cp "$SCRIPT_DIR/docker_entrypoint.sh" "$BUILD_CONTEXT/docker_entrypoint.sh"
REVISION="$(git -C "$PROJECT_ROOT" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || printf 'file-transfer')"
SOURCE_SHA="$(python3 "$REAL_JACKAL_DIR/scripts/deployment_manifest.py" create \
  --package "$BUILD_CONTEXT/package" --output "$BUILD_CONTEXT/source_manifest.json" \
  --revision "$REVISION")"
OUTPUT_IMAGE="${OUTPUT_IMAGE:-moai-jackal-spubert:stability-$(date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)-${SOURCE_SHA:0:12}}"
if docker image inspect "$OUTPUT_IMAGE" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Refusing to replace existing image tag: $OUTPUT_IMAGE (choose a new tag)." >&2
  exit 1
fi
printf 'Base image: %s\nOutput image: %s\nPackage SHA256: %s\n' \
  "$BASE_IMAGE_ID" "$OUTPUT_IMAGE" "$SOURCE_SHA"
docker build --build-arg "BASE_IMAGE=$BASE_PIN_TAG" --build-arg "BASE_IMAGE_ID=$BASE_IMAGE_ID" \
  --build-arg "SOURCE_SHA=$SOURCE_SHA" --build-arg "SOURCE_REVISION=$REVISION" \
  -t "$OUTPUT_IMAGE" "$BUILD_CONTEXT"
printf 'Built %s\nNo ROS nodes or drive commands were started.\n' "$OUTPUT_IMAGE"

**Root cause found for the "moves then stops then moves" (repeated hold) behavior, independent of the above:** it's `/scan` going stale past `safe_path_tracker`'s 0.5s `scan_timeout_sec`, over and over, because the sensor pipeline can't sustain 10Hz. Two real bugs found and fixed in `spu_deploy_docker/context/local_pkgs/mola_bringup/{mola_bringup,scripts}/filterpass.py` (same file duplicated in both dirs - patch both, plus the installed copies in the container: `/root/robot_ws/install/mola_bringup/{local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages,lib}/mola_bringup/filterpass.py`, then kill+relaunch `ros2 run mola_bringup filterpass.py`):
1. The point filter looped over every point in pure Python (`for p in pc2.read_points(...)`) - rewritten to vectorized numpy (`np.frombuffer` + boolean masking), cutting the mask/filter step to ~1ms.

2. The much bigger cost (~54ms/frame on a ~20k-point Livox frame, the dominant chunk of the 100ms budget): assigning a plain `bytes` object to a ROS message's byte-array field (`new_msg.data = selected.tobytes()`) triggers rclpy's per-element Python validation. Assigning `array.array('B', selected.tobytes())` instead matches the fast-path check and takes <1ms - a ~95x speedup on that step alone. **This exact antipattern (`.data = bytes_or_list` on a large ROS array field) is worth grep'ing for elsewhere** (`grep -rn "\.data = " --include=*.py`) - found one more instance, currently inactive/unused, in `spu_data_extractor/realtime_predict_node.py:499` (`msg.data = out.flatten().tolist()` on an OccupancyGrid).
